system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Exide Technologies realized record, fixed ~2018-2020 outcome window (3-5 years after the April 30, 2015 emergence)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The company deregistered from SEC reporting
> shortly after emergence, so there is no post-emergence public 10-K; the realized
> record is traced through the deregistration filing itself and through reputable press.
> This sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was structured at
> closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- Shortly after the Plan's April 30, 2015 Effective Date, the company filed a Form
  15-12B, dated May 1, 2015, certifying termination of registration of its common shares
  under Section 12(g) and suspension of its duty to file reports under Sections 13 and
  15(d) of the Exchange Act, reporting approximately 117 holders of record. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-15-164575, Form 15-12B]
- The company's EDGAR filing history shows no Form 10-K or Form 10-Q filed after
  deregistration; the only subsequent filings are beneficial-ownership disclosures
  (Schedule 13D/13G and Form 3) made by holders of the newly issued securities, the last
  dated February 16, 2016, with no filings of any kind thereafter. [SRC: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000813781.json]
- Consequently there is no audited public financial statement covering the fixed
  ~2018-2020 outcome window (3-5 years after the April 2015 emergence); the realized
  facts below rely on a subsequent bankruptcy filing and reputable press rather than a
  primary annual report.

## Realized record at/beyond the fixed window (press-sourced)
- On May 19, 2020 — just past the outer edge of the fixed window — Exide Holdings, Inc.
  and four affiliated debtors filed voluntary petitions for Chapter 11 relief in the U.S.
  Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware; the filing separated the North American
  business, placed into a court-supervised sale process, from the EMEA/Asia-Pacific
  business, which was offered for sale separately. A company representative was quoted:
  "As it looks today, this is the end of Exide Technologies North America." [SRC: https://www.batteriesinternational.com/2020/05/21/exide-up-for-sale-as-north-american-business-enters-third-chapter-11/]
- The company obtained $40 million in debtor-in-possession financing from a group of
  lenders, including certain existing noteholders, to fund operations during the sale
  process. [SRC: https://www.batteriesinternational.com/2020/05/21/exide-up-for-sale-as-north-american-business-enters-third-chapter-11/]
- The company identified 16 non-performing sites carrying more than $250 million in
  associated costs, with the Vernon, California recycling facility alone accounting for
  $156 million of that figure. [SRC: https://www.batteriesinternational.com/2020/05/21/exide-up-for-sale-as-north-american-business-enters-third-chapter-11/]
- On August 25, 2020, Atlas Holdings completed a court-supervised acquisition, under
  Section 363 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, of substantially all of the operating assets
  of the Americas business of Exide Technologies, LLC, and established two standalone
  successor companies: Stryten Manufacturing (battery manufacturing, headquartered in
  Milton, Georgia, operating seven U.S. manufacturing plants) and Element Resources
  (battery recycling, operating two U.S. recycling plants). [SRC: https://www.atlasholdingsllc.com/news/atlas-holdings-establishes-stryten-manufacturing-following-acquisition-of-asset/]
- Stryten Manufacturing's announced leadership included Tim Vargo as chief executive
  officer, described in the announcement as having previously served as chairman,
  president, and CEO of Exide Technologies — indicating some continuity of prior senior
  management into the successor entity, alongside Mike Judd as president and chief
  operating officer. [SRC: https://www.atlasholdingsllc.com/news/atlas-holdings-establishes-stryten-manufacturing-following-acquisition-of-asset/]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- Aggregated court-docket listings report the 2020 case numbers and presiding judge for
  the Exide Holdings/Exide Technologies, LLC filings, but these were not independently
  confirmed by fetching a court document directly and are recorded here as [UNVERIFIED]. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- No audited public financial statement exists for the fixed ~2018-2020 outcome window,
  so the outcome is coded uncertain on any financial scalar; the best-documented realized
  fact is that, just beyond the five-year mark after emergence, the reorganized company's
  North American business entered a second Chapter 11 case (May 2020) separating it from
  its EMEA/Asia-Pacific operations, followed roughly three months later by a Section 363
  sale of its North American operating assets to Atlas Holdings, which re-launched the
  manufacturing and recycling operations under two new corporate names (Stryten
  Manufacturing and Element Resources) rather than continuing Exide Technologies as an
  independent going concern in North America. [SRC: https://www.batteriesinternational.com/2020/05/21/exide-up-for-sale-as-north-american-business-enters-third-chapter-11/] [SRC: https://www.atlasholdingsllc.com/news/atlas-holdings-establishes-stryten-manufacturing-following-acquisition-of-asset/]

[SLICE END]
